definitions.explanation: Metal blocks with raised letters used in traditional printing. By extension, refers to printed text in general.

definitions.gloss: printed text; print (as opposed to handwriting or speech)
definitions.explanation: Written text that has been printed or published, as distinguished from manuscripts or spoken words.

examples.japanese: {活字|かつじ}⟦{離|ばな}れ→離れ：10003_banare⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}んでいる→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: People are increasingly turning away from print media.
examples.notes: [Note: 活字離れ = decline in reading printed materials]

examples.english: I was moved when I first saw my writing in print.

examples.english: The skill of typesetters who pick up movable type.

examples.english: Old printing type is on display at the museum.

examples.japanese: グーテンベルクは{活字|かつじ}{印刷|いんさつ}を{発明|はつめい}した{人物|じんぶつ}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Gutenberg is known as the person who invented movable type printing.

examples.japanese: {若者|わかもの}の{活字|かつじ}{離|ばな}れが{社会|しゃかい}{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: Young people's move away from print media has become a social issue.

notes:
HISTORICAL CONTEXT: {活字|かつじ} refers to the metal type pieces used in movable type printing, invented in China and later developed in Korea and Europe (Gutenberg). Japan adopted movable type in the late 1500s.

MODERN USAGE:
・{活字|かつじ}{離|ばな}れ (decline in reading print)
・{活字|かつじ}を{追|お}う (to read voraciously)
・{活字|かつじ}{中毒|ちゅうどく} (print addiction - avid reader)
・{活字|かつじ}{文化|ぶんか} (print culture)
・{活字|かつじ}{媒体|ばいたい} (print media)

EXPRESSIONS:
・{活字|かつじ}になる (to be published, to appear in print)
・{活字|かつじ}を{拾|ひろ}う (to set type - traditional printing)

RELATED:
・{印刷|いんさつ} (printing)
・{出版|しゅっぱん} (publishing)
・フォント (font - modern term)
